text.p: Advance Bank Australia Ltd shareholders approved overwhelmingly on Monday the bank's plan to change of its articles of association as a prelude to the proposed merger with St George Bank Ltd.
The change in the bank's articles of association allows a single shareholder to own more than 10 percent of the bank's shares.

Advance Bank chairman Jim Service said shareholders representing 87.78 percent of the issue capital voted in favour of the proposal, while 12.33 percent, including the 10 percent held by trustees of Advance Bank, voted against it.
Shareholders are to vote soon on the bank's capital reduction plan as part of the scheme of arrangement with St George.

Under the merger proposal, St George Bank is to offer Advance Bank ordinary shareholders 0.625 of a new St George Bank ordinary share, A$2.10 in cash from St George and a 20-cent per share special dividend for each Advance Bank share.
The special dividend would be franked to about 60 percent.
Advance Bank ordinary shareholders would also receive an interim fully franked dividend of 20 cents per share.
The offer values Advance at over A$2.6 billion.
The approval means that National Australia Bank Ltd, which had a three percent stake in Advance and 6.8 percent of St George, was unlikely to block the merger.
NAB, which has been widely seen as a potential buyer of regional banks, had not said before today's meeting whether it opposes the merger.
